section.h2: Frequently Asked Questions About Accessing Lu-177-PSMA Therapy in India
section.intro: Lu-177-PSMA is a targeted radioligand therapy used in selected patients with advanced prostate cancer, available at leading Indian centres including Tata Memorial Centre and Apollo Proton Centre. These FAQs explain how it works, who may qualify, and how international patients can access it.

items.a: Lu-177-PSMA therapy is a targeted radioligand treatment for advanced prostate cancer that delivers radiation directly to cancer cells expressing the prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). A molecule that binds PSMA is combined with radioactive Lutetium-177, allowing radiation to concentrate in tumours while limiting damage to healthy tissue. It is generally used for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and is given only after specialist review and suitable PSMA PET imaging.

Lu-177-PSMA works by seeking out prostate cancer cells that carry PSMA on their surface and delivering targeted radiation to them. The therapy is injected into a vein, travels through the bloodstream, and binds to PSMA-positive cells, where Lutetium-177 releases radiation that damages the cancer. Because the radiation acts over a short range, nearby healthy cells are relatively spared. Treatment is planned individually and monitored closely by a nuclear medicine team.

items.q: Which prostate cancers may respond to Lu-177-PSMA?
items.a: Lu-177-PSMA may be considered for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose tumours show strong PSMA uptake on a PSMA PET scan. It is typically discussed after standard treatments such as hormone therapy and chemotherapy have been used or considered. Response depends on cancer type, extent of spread, PSMA expression, previous treatment, and overall health, so suitability should always be confirmed by a qualified oncology and nuclear medicine team.

items.q: What is PSMA and why does it matter for this therapy?
items.a: PSMA, or prostate-specific membrane antigen, is a protein found in high amounts on most prostate cancer cells. It matters because Lu-177-PSMA therapy relies on this protein as a target, using it to guide radiation precisely to cancer cells. Before treatment, a PSMA PET scan checks whether the cancer shows enough PSMA uptake. Patients whose tumours express little PSMA may not be suitable candidates, so imaging is an essential first step.

items.q: Who is eligible for Lu-177-PSMA therapy in India?
items.a: Eligibility for Lu-177-PSMA therapy is decided after specialist review and PSMA PET imaging, usually for patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Doctors also assess kidney function, blood counts, bone marrow reserve, previous treatments, and overall fitness. It may be suitable for selected patients when standard options have progressed or are unsuitable. Final decisions depend on cancer type, stage, biomarker profile, and specialist assessment by the treating medical team.

items.q: What tests are needed before starting Lu-177-PSMA therapy?
items.a: A PSMA PET scan is the key test needed before Lu-177-PSMA therapy, confirming that the cancer expresses enough PSMA to be targeted. Doctors also review blood tests for kidney function, blood counts, and PSA levels, along with imaging of the whole body. Previous pathology and treatment records are assessed too. These tests help the medical team judge whether the therapy may be suitable and how it should be planned and monitored.

Lu-177-PSMA therapy is given as an injection into a vein, usually in a specialised nuclear medicine unit. Treatment is typically delivered in several cycles spaced a few weeks apart, with the exact number decided by the treating team based on response and tolerance. Patients may stay under observation for radiation safety after each dose. Blood tests and scans are done between cycles to monitor benefit and side effects and to guide further treatment.

items.q: What are the possible side effects of Lu-177-PSMA therapy?
items.a: Common side effects of Lu-177-PSMA therapy include dry mouth, tiredness, nausea, and temporary drops in blood counts. Because the therapy is radioactive, brief radiation precautions may be advised after each dose. Less commonly, kidney function or bone marrow may be affected, which is why regular monitoring is important. Side effects vary between patients and should be discussed with the treating team, who will weigh possible benefits against risks before and during treatment.

Lu-177-PSMA therapy is generally considered well tolerated in appropriately selected patients, but no cancer treatment is risk-free. Safety depends on kidney function, bone marrow reserve, PSMA expression, and overall health, all of which are checked beforehand. Radiation precautions are followed to protect patients and those around them. Regular blood tests and imaging help detect problems early. The treating oncology and nuclear medicine team monitors each patient closely to manage risks and adjust care.

items.q: How much does Lu-177-PSMA therapy cost in India?
items.a: The cost of Lu-177-PSMA therapy in India varies and cannot be quoted as a single fixed price. It depends on the hospital, the number of treatment cycles, imaging such as PSMA PET, supportive care, length of stay, and any complications. India is often chosen because advanced cancer care may be more affordable than in some countries. A personalised estimate should be obtained from the treating centre after reviewing the patient's medical records.

items.q: Is Lu-177-PSMA therapy available at Tata Memorial Centre?
items.a: Tata Memorial Centre in Mumbai is a leading Indian cancer institution with nuclear medicine expertise and is one of the centres associated with PSMA-targeted therapies. Availability of Lu-177-PSMA at any specific time depends on the centre's current protocols, radiopharmaceutical supply, and individual patient eligibility. Patients interested in treatment there should confirm current availability, referral requirements, and waiting times directly with the hospital, as access is decided after medical review and PSMA imaging.

items.q: Is Lu-177-PSMA therapy available at Apollo Proton Centre?
items.a: Apollo Proton Cancer Centre in Chennai is a specialised oncology facility with advanced imaging and nuclear medicine services that may offer PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy. Whether Lu-177-PSMA is available for a particular patient depends on current hospital protocols, radiopharmaceutical supply, and individual eligibility confirmed through PSMA PET imaging and specialist review. Prospective patients should verify current availability, appointment processes, and cost estimates directly with the centre before making travel or treatment plans.

Lu-177-PSMA therapy is offered in several countries, including India, and is available at selected specialised centres in parts of Europe, Australia, and North America. Availability and approval status differ between countries and may change over time. India is often considered by international patients because established centres provide the therapy alongside supporting imaging. Patients should confirm current availability, regulatory approval, and eligibility with a specific centre, as access always depends on medical review.

items.q: How does Lu-177-PSMA compare with chemotherapy for prostate cancer?
items.a: Lu-177-PSMA and chemotherapy work in different ways and are not interchangeable for every patient. Lu-177-PSMA targets PSMA-positive cancer cells with radiation, while chemotherapy circulates broadly to kill dividing cells. In advanced prostate cancer, they may be used at different points in the treatment journey rather than as direct substitutes. Which option is appropriate depends on cancer stage, PSMA expression, previous treatment, and overall health, and should be decided by the treating oncology team.

items.q: Are there clinical trials for Lu-177-PSMA therapy in India?
items.a: Clinical trials involving PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy do take place at some Indian and international centres, but availability changes over time. Trials often have strict inclusion and exclusion criteria, and enrolment cannot be guaranteed. Eligibility is decided only after medical record review and investigator assessment, and joining a trial does not guarantee benefit. Patients interested in trials should ask their treating centre about current studies and discuss the possible risks and requirements involved.

items.q: Can Lu-177-PSMA be repeated if the cancer progresses again?
items.a: Lu-177-PSMA therapy may be repeated in selected patients if the cancer initially responded and later progressed, but this is not always possible. Repeat treatment depends on remaining PSMA expression, kidney function, bone marrow reserve, cumulative radiation exposure, and overall health. A fresh PSMA PET scan and specialist review are usually needed before considering further cycles. The decision to re-treat should always be made by the treating oncology and nuclear medicine team.

items.q: How can international patients access Lu-177-PSMA therapy in India?
items.a: International patients can access Lu-177-PSMA therapy in India by first sharing their medical reports with a chosen centre for review and eligibility assessment. Access depends on hospital acceptance, PSMA imaging results, medical fitness, visa approval, and travel arrangements, none of which can be guaranteed in advance. Patients usually need a treatment plan and cost estimate before travelling. Planning follow-up care and radiation safety precautions for the return journey is also important.

items.q: What medical reports are needed to plan treatment from abroad?
items.a: International patients should prepare recent medical reports including prostate cancer pathology, PSA history, prior treatment details, and imaging such as PSMA PET, CT, or bone scans. Kidney function and blood count results are also helpful. These records allow the treating centre to assess whether Lu-177-PSMA may be suitable and to provide a preliminary plan and cost estimate. A second opinion may be arranged, but final eligibility is confirmed only after full specialist review.

items.q: How does CancerFax help patients with Lu-177-PSMA therapy in India?
items.a: CancerFax helps patients organise medical reports, identify relevant specialists or treatment centres such as Tata Memorial Centre and Apollo Proton Centre, estimate possible costs, and coordinate second opinions, appointments, travel, visa, and follow-up support. Treatment decisions are always made by the qualified oncology team after reviewing the patient's diagnosis, stage, biomarkers, previous treatment, and overall health. Access to Lu-177-PSMA therapy depends on medical review and cannot be guaranteed.
